@panels.doc.common.copyToClipboard.context: Tooltip of the copy icon button in the header of a document panel (command result, BASIC listing, script output); copies the panel's whole text.

@panels.doc.common.goTo.context: Label in front of the address box in a document panel's header (binary file viewer, disassembly); type an address and press Enter to jump there.

@panels.doc.common.refreshNow.context: Tooltip of the refresh icon button in the header of the BASIC listing and disassembly panels; re-reads the machine's memory at once.

panels.doc.unknownFile.noViewer: This file type has no associated viewer

@panels.doc.unknownFile.noViewer.context: Message filling the document panel opened for a file whose type Klive cannot display. Not an error: the file is fine.

panels.doc.commandResult.noBuffer: This command produced no output buffer.

@panels.doc.commandResult.noBuffer.context: Error message filling a command-result document panel when the IDE command that opened it supplied no output to show.

panels.doc.commandResult.copied: Command output text copied to the clipboard

@panels.doc.commandResult.copied.context: Status-bar message after the copy button of a command-result document panel copied the command's output.

@panels.doc.binViewer.layout8x1.context: Option of the dump-layout dropdown in the binary file viewer: 8 bytes per row in one column. 'B' is bytes, 'col' is column; keep it short.

@panels.doc.binViewer.layout8x2.context: Option of the dump-layout dropdown in the binary file viewer: two columns of 8 bytes per row. 'B' is bytes, 'col' is column; keep it short.

@panels.doc.binViewer.layout16x1.context: Option of the dump-layout dropdown in the binary file viewer: 16 bytes per row in one column. 'B' is bytes, 'col' is column; keep it short.

@panels.doc.binViewer.noContent.context: Message filling the binary file viewer when the opened file is empty.

panels.doc.binViewer.tooLarge: File is too large to display ({sizeMb} MB). Maximum supported size is {maxMb} MB.

@panels.doc.binViewer.tooLarge.context: Message filling the binary file viewer when the opened file is bigger than it can show.

placeholders.sizeMb: The file's size in megabytes, already formatted with two decimals, e.g. '5.25'
placeholders.maxMb: The largest size the viewer shows, in megabytes (4)

@panels.doc.binViewer.decimal.context: Label of a switch in the binary file viewer's header: show byte values and addresses in decimal instead of hexadecimal.

@panels.doc.binViewer.decimalTitle.context: Tooltip of the 'Decimal' switch in the binary file viewer's header.

@panels.doc.binViewer.view.context: Label in front of the dump-layout dropdown (bytes per row) in the binary file viewer's header.

@panels.doc.binViewer.chars.context: Label of a switch in the binary file viewer's header: show each row's bytes as characters too. Short for 'characters'.

@panels.doc.binViewer.charsTitle.context: Tooltip of the 'Chars' switch in the binary file viewer's header.

@panels.doc.staticMemory.showAll.context: Label of a switch above a memory dump embedded in a file viewer (e.g. a tape block's data): show every byte instead of only the leading ones.

panels.doc.staticMemory.showingLeading: (Showing only the leading {count, plural, one {# byte} other {# bytes}})

@panels.doc.staticMemory.showingLeading.context: Note next to the 'Show all' switch above a memory dump embedded in a file viewer, while only the first bytes are shown.

@panels.doc.imageViewer.fitOriginal.context: Option of the sizing dropdown in the image viewer's header: show the image at its own size (the zoom buttons then apply).

@panels.doc.imageViewer.fitWidth.context: Option of the sizing dropdown in the image viewer's header: scale the image to the panel's width.

@panels.doc.imageViewer.fitPage.context: Option of the sizing dropdown in the image viewer's header: scale the whole image to fit inside the panel.

@panels.doc.imageViewer.noContent.context: Message filling the image viewer when the opened image file is empty.

panels.doc.imageViewer.decodeFailed: This file could not be decoded as an image ({name}).

@panels.doc.imageViewer.decodeFailed.context: Error message filling the image viewer when the file is corrupt or in a format the viewer cannot show.

panels.doc.imageViewer.decodeFailedUnnam: This file could not be decoded as an image.

@panels.doc.imageViewer.decodeFailedUnna.context: Error message filling the image viewer when the file is corrupt or in a format the viewer cannot show, and its name is not known.

@panels.doc.imageViewer.zoomOut.context: Tooltip of the zoom-out icon button in the image viewer's header.

@panels.doc.imageViewer.zoomIn.context: Tooltip of the zoom-in icon button in the image viewer's header.

@panels.doc.imageViewer.resetZoom.context: Tooltip of the zoom readout (e.g. '2×') between the zoom buttons of the image viewer; clicking it returns to the image's own size.

@panels.doc.imageViewer.previewAlt.context: Alternative text (screen readers) of the image shown in the image viewer.

@panels.doc.scriptOutput.stop.context: Tooltip of the stop icon button in the header of a script's output panel; cancels the running script.

@panels.doc.scriptOutput.openFile.context: Tooltip of an icon button in the header of a script's output panel; opens the script's source file in an editor.

@panels.doc.scriptOutput.clear.context: Tooltip of an icon button in the header of a script's output panel; empties the output.

panels.doc.scriptOutput.copied: Script output copied to the clipboard

@panels.doc.scriptOutput.copied.context: Status-bar message after the copy button of a script's output panel copied the output.

@panels.doc.scriptOutput.autoScrollOn.context: Tooltip of the lock icon button in a script's output panel while auto scrolling is off; clicking makes the panel follow new output.

@panels.doc.scriptOutput.autoScrollOff.context: Tooltip of the lock icon button in a script's output panel while auto scrolling is on; clicking keeps the view where it is when new output arrives.

@panels.doc.scriptOutput.lines.context: Readout in the header of a script's output panel: how many output lines the script wrote so far.

@panels.doc.scriptOutput.statusRunning.context: Status readout in the header of a script's output panel while the script runs. Keep the brackets.

@panels.doc.scriptOutput.statusStopped.context: Status readout in the header of a script's output panel after the user stopped the script. Keep the brackets.

@panels.doc.scriptOutput.statusError.context: Status readout in the header of a script's output panel after the script failed. Keep the brackets.

@panels.doc.scriptOutput.statusCompleted.context: Status readout in the header of a script's output panel after the script finished normally. Keep the brackets.

@panels.doc.basic.emptyProgram.context: Message filling the BASIC Listing panel when the emulated machine's memory holds no BASIC program.

panels.doc.basic.osNotInitialized: Machine OS has not been initialized yet

@panels.doc.basic.osNotInitialized.context: Message filling the BASIC Listing panel before the emulated machine's ROM has finished starting up (no BASIC program area exists yet).

@panels.doc.basic.refreshed.context: Status-bar message after the refresh button of the BASIC Listing panel re-read the program.

panels.doc.basic.copied: BASIC listing copied to the clipboard

@panels.doc.basic.copied.context: Status-bar message after the copy button of the BASIC Listing panel copied the program text.

@panels.doc.basic.autoRefresh.context: Label of a switch in the BASIC Listing panel's header: re-read the program periodically while the machine runs. Keep the colon if your language uses one.

@panels.doc.basic.autoRefreshTitle.context: Tooltip of the 'Auto Refresh' switch in the BASIC Listing panel's header.

@panels.doc.basic.showCodes.context: Label of a switch in the BASIC Listing panel's header: also show the control codes (colour, position) embedded in the program lines.

@panels.doc.basic.showCodesTitle.context: Tooltip of the 'Show Non-Printable' switch in the BASIC Listing panel's header.

@panels.doc.basic.spectrumFont.context: Label of a switch in the BASIC Listing panel's header (ZX Spectrum machines): draw the listing with the machine's own character set. 'ZX Spectrum' is a computer's name.

@panels.doc.basic.sinclairFont.context: Label of a switch in the BASIC Listing panel's header (ZX80/ZX81 machines): draw the listing with the machine's own character set. 'Sinclair' is the maker's name.

panels.doc.basic.fontTitle: Use the ZX Spectrum's font (the Sinclair font) to display the list

@panels.doc.basic.fontTitle.context: Tooltip of the font switch in the BASIC Listing panel's header.

@panels.doc.breakpoint.type.execute.context: Breakpoint kind, shown in brackets after the address in the tooltip of a breakpoint glyph (disassembly gutter, Breakpoints panel): stops when the CPU executes the instruction there.

@panels.doc.breakpoint.type.memoryRead.context: Breakpoint kind, shown in brackets after the address in the tooltip of a breakpoint glyph: stops when the CPU reads that memory address.

@panels.doc.breakpoint.type.memoryWrite.context: Breakpoint kind, shown in brackets after the address in the tooltip of a breakpoint glyph: stops when the CPU writes that memory address.

@panels.doc.breakpoint.type.ioRead.context: Breakpoint kind, shown in brackets after the port in the tooltip of a breakpoint glyph: stops when the CPU reads that I/O port.

@panels.doc.breakpoint.type.ioWrite.context: Breakpoint kind, shown in brackets after the port in the tooltip of a breakpoint glyph: stops when the CPU writes that I/O port.

@panels.doc.breakpoint.type.nextRegWrite.context: Breakpoint kind (ZX Spectrum Next), shown in brackets in the tooltip of a breakpoint glyph: stops when a Next register is written. 'NextReg' is a hardware name; keep it.

@panels.doc.breakpoint.type.copper.context: Breakpoint kind (ZX Spectrum Next), shown in brackets in the tooltip of a breakpoint glyph: stops when the Copper co-processor completes an instruction. 'Copper' is a hardware name; keep it.

@panels.doc.breakpoint.type.spriteWrite.context: Breakpoint kind (ZX Spectrum Next), shown in brackets in the tooltip of a breakpoint glyph: stops when a hardware sprite's attributes are written.

panels.doc.breakpoint.heading: {address} ({type})

@panels.doc.breakpoint.heading.context: First line of the tooltip of a breakpoint glyph: where the breakpoint is and its kind, e.g. '$8000 (execute)'. Change only the bracket style if your language needs to.

placeholders.address: The breakpoint's address, port or source line, e.g. '$8000' or 'ROM0:$0038'; never translated
placeholders.type: The breakpoint's kind, one of the panels.doc.breakpoint.type.* messages

@panels.doc.breakpoint.headingMasked.context: First line of the tooltip of an I/O breakpoint glyph whose port is matched through a mask, e.g. '$00FE /$00FF (I/O read)'. Change only the bracket style if your language needs to.

placeholders.address: The I/O port, e.g. '$00FE'; never translated
placeholders.mask: The port mask, e.g. '$00FF'; never translated
placeholders.type: The breakpoint's kind, one of the panels.doc.breakpoint.type.* messages

panels.doc.breakpoint.hint.readOnly: Edit the comment and rebuild to change it

@panels.doc.breakpoint.hint.readOnly.context: Line of the tooltip of a breakpoint glyph whose breakpoint comes from a special comment in the source code (LOGPOINT, ASSERTION, WPMEM): it cannot be changed here.

@panels.doc.breakpoint.hint.remove.context: Line of the tooltip of a breakpoint glyph in the gutter of the disassembly or a breakpoint list.

@panels.doc.breakpoint.hint.set.context: Line of the tooltip of the empty breakpoint gutter of a disassembly row.

@panels.doc.breakpoint.hint.edit.context: Line of the tooltip of a breakpoint glyph; double-clicking opens the breakpoint editor dialog.

@panels.doc.breakpoint.hint.runHere.context: Line of the tooltip of the breakpoint gutter: clicking it with the modifier key held runs the machine until it reaches this row.

placeholders.modifier: The keyboard modifier's name: 'Cmd' on macOS, 'Ctrl' elsewhere; never translated

@panels.doc.breakpoint.hint.removeOneSho.context: Line of the tooltip of a one-shot breakpoint glyph (a breakpoint removed after it stops once). 'Shift' is the key's name.

panels.doc.breakpoint.hint.makeOneShot: Shift-click to make it stop here once

@panels.doc.breakpoint.hint.makeOneShot.context: Line of the tooltip of a breakpoint glyph: Shift-click turns the breakpoint into a one-shot that is removed after it stops once.

@panels.doc.breakpoint.hint.setOneShot.context: Line of the tooltip of the empty breakpoint gutter: Shift-click sets a one-shot breakpoint, removed after it stops once.

@panels.doc.breakpoint.hint.enable.context: Line of the tooltip of the checkbox next to a disabled breakpoint in a breakpoint list.

@panels.doc.breakpoint.hint.disable.context: Line of the tooltip of the checkbox next to an enabled breakpoint in a breakpoint list.

panels.doc.rowMenu.label: Label...

@panels.doc.rowMenu.label.context: Context-menu item of a disassembly row (right-click): opens a box to name the row's address with a label in the active annotation set.

@panels.doc.rowMenu.labelRom.context: Context-menu item of a ROM row in the disassembly: opens a box to name the address with a label, stored in the user's editable copy of the ROM's annotations.

@panels.doc.rowMenu.synopsis.context: Context-menu item of a disassembly row: opens a box to write a comment block shown above the row.

@panels.doc.rowMenu.synopsisRom.context: Context-menu item of a ROM row in the disassembly: opens a box to write a comment block shown above the row, stored in the user's editable copy of the ROM's annotations.

@panels.doc.rowMenu.comment.context: Context-menu item of a disassembly row: opens a box to write a comment shown at the end of the row.

@panels.doc.rowMenu.commentRom.context: Context-menu item of a ROM row in the disassembly: opens a box to write a comment shown at the end of the row, stored in the user's editable copy of the ROM's annotations.

@panels.doc.rowMenu.operandLabel.context: Context-menu item of a disassembly row: opens a box to name the value or address the instruction's operand uses.

@panels.doc.rowMenu.operandLabelRom.context: Context-menu item of a ROM row in the disassembly: opens a box to name the instruction's operand, stored in the user's editable copy of the ROM's annotations.

@panels.doc.rowMenu.gotoDefinition.context: Context-menu item of a disassembly row: scrolls to the address the instruction's operand label names.

@panels.doc.rowMenu.openRomAnnotations.context: Context-menu item of a ROM row in the disassembly: opens the editor of the user's editable copy of the ROM's labels and comments.

@panels.doc.rowMenu.startRomAnnotations.context: Context-menu item of a ROM row in the disassembly when the user has no editable copy of the ROM's labels and comments yet: creates one.

@panels.doc.rowMenu.removeBreakpoint.context: Context-menu item of a disassembly row that has a breakpoint.

@panels.doc.rowMenu.keepAfterStop.context: Context-menu item of a disassembly row with a one-shot breakpoint: makes it an ordinary breakpoint that stays after the machine stops on it.

@panels.doc.rowMenu.removeAfterStop.context: Context-menu item of a disassembly row with a breakpoint: makes it a one-shot, removed the first time the machine stops on it.

@panels.doc.rowMenu.addBreakpoint.context: Context-menu item of a disassembly row without a breakpoint.

@panels.doc.rowMenu.addOneShot.context: Context-menu item of a disassembly row: sets a breakpoint that is removed the first time the machine stops on it.

@panels.doc.rowMenu.runToHere.context: Context-menu item of a disassembly row: runs the machine until it reaches this instruction, without leaving a breakpoint.

@panels.doc.rowMenu.editBreakpoint.context: Context-menu item of a disassembly row: opens the breakpoint editor dialog for the row's breakpoint.

@panels.doc.rowMenu.showAsGraphics.context: Context-menu item of a disassembly row: opens the graphics finder showing the memory from this address as pixels.

@panels.doc.disassembly.decimal.context: Label of a switch in the disassembly panel's header: show numbers in decimal instead of hexadecimal.

@panels.doc.disassembly.decimalTitle.context: Tooltip of the 'Decimal' switch in the disassembly panel's header.

@panels.doc.disassembly.sysVars.context: Label of a switch in the disassembly panel's header: show the names of the ROM's system variables (e.g. ERR_SP) in place of their addresses. Short for 'system variables'.

panels.doc.disassembly.sysVarsTitle: Show system variable names in operands?

@panels.doc.disassembly.sysVarsTitle.context: Tooltip of the 'Sys vars' switch in the disassembly and memory panels: show the names of the ROM's system variables in place of their addresses.

@panels.doc.disassembly.romLabels.context: Label of a switch in the disassembly panel's header (machines with annotated ROMs): show the ROM's labels, comments and data regions.

panels.doc.disassembly.romLabelsTitle: Show the ROM's labels, comments and data regions?

@panels.doc.disassembly.romLabelsTitle.context: Tooltip of the 'ROM labels' switch in the disassembly panel's header.

@panels.doc.disassembly.followPc.context: Label of a switch in the disassembly panel's header: keep the listing around the instruction the CPU executes next. 'PC' is the Z80's program counter register; keep it.

@panels.doc.disassembly.followPcTitle.context: Tooltip of the 'Follow PC' switch in the disassembly panel's header. 'PC' is the Z80's program counter register; keep it.

@panels.doc.disassembly.ram.context: Label of a switch in the disassembly panel's header: include RAM in the listing. 'RAM' is a hardware term; change it only if your language has its own.

@panels.doc.disassembly.ramTitle.context: Tooltip of the 'RAM' switch in the disassembly panel's header.

@panels.doc.disassembly.screen.context: Label of a switch in the disassembly panel's header: include the screen memory in the listing.

@panels.doc.disassembly.screenTitle.context: Tooltip of the 'Screen' switch in the disassembly panel's header: include the screen memory area in the listing.

@panels.doc.disassembly.bank.context: Label of a switch in the disassembly panel's header: show which memory bank each row's address is in.

@panels.doc.disassembly.bankTitle.context: Tooltip of the 'Bank' switch in the disassembly panel's header.

@panels.doc.disassembly.goToPc.context: Tooltip of the arrow icon button in the disassembly panel's header: scrolls to the instruction the CPU executes next. 'PC' is the Z80's program counter register; keep it.

@panels.doc.disassembly.fullView.context: Label of a switch in the disassembly panel's second header row: list the whole 64K address space instead of one memory bank.

@panels.doc.disassembly.fullViewTitle.context: Tooltip of the '64K View' switch in the disassembly panel's header.

@panels.doc.disassembly.selectBank.context: Label in front of the memory-bank chooser in the disassembly panel's header.

@panels.doc.disassembly.offset.context: Label in front of the dropdown choosing the start offset inside the selected bank in the disassembly panel's header.

panels.doc.copper.notAvailable: The Copper is available on the ZX Spectrum Next

@panels.doc.copper.notAvailable.context: Message filling the Copper List panel on a machine other than the ZX Spectrum Next. 'Copper' is the name of the Next's display co-processor; keep it.

@panels.doc.copper.clickToExpand.context: Hint at the end of a folded row of the Copper List panel that stands for a run of NOP instructions; clicking shows them one by one.

@panels.doc.copper.removeBreakpointOn.context: Tooltip of the breakpoint gutter of a Copper List row that has a breakpoint.

placeholders.index: The Copper instruction's index in the list, e.g. '#012'; never translated

@panels.doc.copper.stopWhenCompletes.context: Tooltip of the empty breakpoint gutter of a Copper List row: clicking sets a breakpoint that stops the machine once the Copper has done this instruction.

placeholders.index: The Copper instruction's index in the list, e.g. '#012'; never translated

panels.doc.copper.waitNeverMatches: This WAIT never matches under the current timing

@panels.doc.copper.waitNeverMatches.context: Tooltip of a Copper List row's explanation, shown in warning colour: the WAIT instruction waits for a raster position this machine's video timing never reaches. 'WAIT' is the instruction's name; keep it.

panels.doc.copper.waitOutOfOrder: This WAIT is for an earlier line than the WAIT before it: in a looping mode it waits for the next frame

@panels.doc.copper.waitOutOfOrder.context: Tooltip of a Copper List row's explanation, shown in warning colour. 'WAIT' is the instruction's name; keep it.

@panels.doc.copper.hitAt.context: Note after the explanation of the Copper List row where the breakpoint stopped: the raster line and horizontal position at that moment. 'hc' is the hardware's horizontal counter; keep it.

@panels.doc.copper.sourcePatched.context: First line of the tooltip of a Copper List row's source column when the instruction in memory differs from the one assembled from that source line.

placeholders.source: The source file name and line, e.g. 'effects.copper:12'
placeholders.word: The instruction word the assembler produced, in hex, e.g. '$8012'

@panels.doc.copper.sourceMatched.context: Second line of the tooltip of a Copper List row's source column: how many of the block's assembled instructions were found in memory.

placeholders.total: The number of instructions the block holds

@panels.doc.copper.followPc.context: Label of a switch in the Copper List panel's header: keep the Copper's next instruction in view. 'PC' is the Copper's program counter; keep it.

panels.doc.copper.followPcTitle: Keep the Copper's PC in view

@panels.doc.copper.followPcTitle.context: Tooltip of the 'Follow PC' switch in the Copper List panel's header. 'PC' is the Copper's program counter; keep it.

@panels.doc.copper.source.context: Label of a switch in the Copper List panel's header: show the source line each instruction was assembled from.

panels.doc.copper.sourceTitle: Show the .copper source line each instruction was assembled from

@panels.doc.copper.sourceTitle.context: Tooltip of the 'Source' switch in the Copper List panel's header. '.copper' is a file extension; keep it.

@panels.doc.copper.hexWait.context: Label of a switch in the Copper List panel's header: show the operands of WAIT instructions in hexadecimal. 'WAIT' is the instruction's name; keep it.

@panels.doc.copper.hexWaitTitle.context: Tooltip of the 'Hex WAIT' switch in the Copper List panel's header. 'WAIT' is the instruction's name; keep it.

panels.doc.copper.step: Step Copper: run until the Copper completes its next instruction

@panels.doc.copper.step.context: Tooltip of the step icon button in the Copper List panel's header. 'Copper' is the co-processor's name; keep it.

@panels.doc.copper.rulerTick.context: Tooltip of the raster ruler beside the Copper List while the pointer is on a WAIT's tick: which instruction waits for which raster line.

placeholders.line: The raster line the WAIT waits for

@panels.doc.copper.rulerTickNeverMatches.context: Tooltip of the raster ruler beside the Copper List while the pointer is on the tick of a WAIT that never matches under the current video timing.

placeholders.line: The raster line the WAIT waits for

@panels.doc.copper.menu.removeBreakpoint.context: Context-menu item of a Copper List row that has a breakpoint.

@panels.doc.copper.menu.addBreakpoint.context: Context-menu item of a Copper List row: stop the machine once the Copper has done this instruction.

@panels.doc.copper.menu.editBreakpoint.context: Context-menu item of a Copper List row with a breakpoint: opens the breakpoint editor dialog.

@panels.doc.copper.menu.runToHere.context: Context-menu item of a Copper List row: runs the machine until the Copper has done this instruction.

@panels.doc.copper.menu.goToSource.context: Context-menu item of a Copper List row: opens the source file at the line the instruction was assembled from.

placeholders.source: The source file name and line, e.g. 'effects.copper:12'

panels.doc.dsk.unreadable: This file could not be read as a .dsk disk image.

@panels.doc.dsk.unreadable.context: Error message filling the disk image viewer when the opened file is not a valid disk image. '.dsk' is a file extension; keep it.

panels.doc.dsk.error.notDsk: This file is not a .dsk disk image: it starts with neither the standard nor the extended DSK signature.

@panels.doc.dsk.error.notDsk.context: Error filling the disk image viewer: the file does not start like a .dsk file. '.dsk' and 'DSK' are file-format names; keep them.

panels.doc.dsk.error.badHeader: The disk image's Disk-Info block is damaged.

@panels.doc.dsk.error.badHeader.context: Error filling the disk image viewer: the file's header block is damaged. 'Disk-Info' is the name of a block in the file format; keep it.

panels.doc.dsk.error.badSides: The disk image says it has {sides} sides; a floppy disk has one or two.

@panels.doc.dsk.error.badSides.context: Error filling the disk image viewer: the file's header gives an impossible number of disk sides.

placeholders.sides: The number of sides the file declares, e.g. 80

panels.doc.dsk.error.badTracks: The disk image says it has {tracks} tracks per side, more than a .dsk file can hold.

@panels.doc.dsk.error.badTracks.context: Error filling the disk image viewer: the file's header gives an impossible number of tracks.

placeholders.tracks: The number of tracks per side the file declares, e.g. 0 or 119

panels.doc.dsk.error.truncated: The disk image is cut short: its tracks need {needed} bytes, but the file has only {length}.

@panels.doc.dsk.error.truncated.context: Error filling the disk image viewer: the file ends before the tracks its header lists.

placeholders.needed: How many bytes the file should have at least, e.g. 194816
placeholders.length: How many bytes the file has, e.g. 190180

panels.doc.dsk.error.missingTrackInfo: Track {cylinder} on side {side} has no Track-Info block (at byte {offset}): the image is damaged.

@panels.doc.dsk.error.missingTrackInfo.context: Error filling the disk image viewer: a track's header block is missing. 'Track-Info' is the name of a block in the file format; keep it.

placeholders.offset: Where in the file the block should be, in bytes

panels.doc.dsk.error.badTrack: Track {track} lists {sectors} sectors, more than its block in the file holds.

@panels.doc.dsk.error.badTrack.context: Error filling the disk image viewer: a track says it holds more sectors than fit in its part of the file.

placeholders.track: The track's index in the file, from 0
placeholders.sectors: The number of sectors the track lists

@panels.doc.dsk.sides.context: Label of a value in the disk image viewer's header: how many sides the floppy disk has.

@panels.doc.dsk.tracks.context: Label of a value in the disk image viewer's header: how many tracks the floppy disk has.

@panels.doc.dsk.diskFormat.context: Label of a value in the disk image viewer's header: the image's format (CPC or Extended CPC, which are format names).

@panels.doc.dsk.showSurface.context: Label of a switch in the disk image viewer's header: show the disk's physical layout (gaps, sync marks, raw bytes) instead of its tracks and sectors.

@panels.doc.dsk.showSurfaceTitle.context: Tooltip of the 'Show surface view' switch in the disk image viewer's header.

@panels.doc.dsk.genericInfo.context: Title of a collapsible section of the disk image viewer's surface view: facts about the whole disk.

@panels.doc.dsk.density.context: Label of a value in the disk image viewer: the floppy's recording density (a hardware term such as 'DoubleDensity', shown untranslated).

@panels.doc.dsk.weakSectors.context: Label of a yes/no flag in the disk image viewer: whether any sector holds weak (copy-protection) data that reads differently each time.

@panels.doc.dsk.total.context: Label of a value in the disk image viewer's surface view: the disk's whole physical size in bytes.

@panels.doc.dsk.totalTitle.context: Tooltip of the 'Total' value in the disk image viewer's surface view.

@panels.doc.dsk.bytesPerTrackTitle.context: Tooltip of the 'B/T' value in the disk image viewer's surface view ('B/T' itself stays untranslated).

@panels.doc.dsk.trackLengthTitle.context: Tooltip of the 'TLen' value in the disk image viewer's surface view ('TLen' itself stays untranslated).

@panels.doc.dsk.trackTitle.context: Title of a collapsible section of the disk image viewer's surface view, one per physical track.

panels.doc.dsk.trackHeader: Track header (GAP0 + Sync + Index + GAP1, {count, plural, one {# byte} other {# bytes}})

@panels.doc.dsk.trackHeader.context: Caption above the raw bytes of a track's header in the disk image viewer's surface view. GAP0, Sync, Index and GAP1 are floppy-format field names; keep them.

placeholders.count: How many bytes the header holds

placeholders.unit: The time unit's symbol, e.g. 'T' for T-states; never translated

placeholders.unit: The time unit's symbol, e.g. 'T' for T-states; never translated

panels.doc.profiler.col.exclusiveTitle: The time of these calls in their own code

@panels.doc.profiler.col.exclusiveTitle.context: Tooltip of the 'Excl.' column header in the Profiler's call tree.
